item.title: China defends jailing Swedish-Chinese bookseller after UN release call
item.description: China rejected on Thursday any "interference" in its judicial sovereignty after a United Nations working group called for the immediate release of jailed Chinese-Swedish bookseller Gui Minhai.

item.title: Swedish word of the day: ljus
item.description: Today's Swedish word is one we all need this time of the year.

item.title: 'Contrary to human dignity': Swedish Church slams plan to revoke permanent residence
item.description: The Church of Sweden has formally rejected a government inquiry's proposal that would see more than 100,000 people stripped of their permanent residency permits, condemning the proposal as "unreasonable", "disproportionate", and arguing it fails to protect human dignity.

item.title: Saints, spooks, and eyeballs: An immigrant's view of Lucia in Sweden
item.description: It's mid-December and in Sweden that means Lucia: groups of white-robed people singing with candles on their heads. But what exactly is this strangely beautiful (and beautifully eerie) celebration about, and where did it come from?

item.title: IN PICTURES: Sweden's contest for the year's best gingerbread house
item.description: The Swedish Centre for Architecture and Design (ArkDes) runs an annual competition for the best 'pepparkakshus' or gingerbread house. Which one do you think should win this year?

item.title: Swedish government finalises bill on hiking work permit salary threshold
item.description: Sweden's government has finalised the text of a new law which will see the minimum eligible salary for a work permit hiked to 33,390 kronor a month from next June, but as yet there is no timetable on when it will be voted on by parliament.

item.title: 'Our Christmas ham has run away': Ten of Sweden's best holiday hits
item.description: Sick of Last Christmas and All I Want for Christmas is You? We've put together a list of Swedish Christmas songs, including standard hits and more unusual offerings, for you to add to your playlist this year.

item.title: Swedish word of the day: lussekatt
item.description: Will you have a lussekatt this weekend? Or two?

item.title: Moderate youth chair calls for Sweden to adjust 'track change' law
item.description: The Moderate Party's youth wing has called for a law removing the right of asylum seekers to "change track" and instead apply for a work permit to be changed so that more who have managed to get stable jobs are allowed to stay in Sweden.

item.title: GOATWATCH: Here's how you can livestream Sweden's Christmas goat
item.description: The Christmas Goat in the Swedish city of Gävle has become a worldwide symbol of the season for many who eagerly follow news of the straw goat to see if it survives until Christmas day. Here's where you can watch it online.
